day_shape: 96 items: UK sanctions Houthi leadership after Red Sea escalation, IDF kills Hamas internal security chief Naim Abu Nahal in Gaza City, Katz says Iran developing chemical weapons, UKMTO reports three vessels struck in Strait of Hormuz, heavy IRGC retaliation threats from Gen. Izadi.

threads.label: Houthi-Saudi escalation and UK sanctions
threads.summary: The UK Foreign Office announced new sanctions against Houthi leaders following attacks inside Yemen and against Saudi Arabia, while Secretary Rubio called Saudi FM Prince Faisal to condemn Iran-backed Houthi strikes on civilian and energy infrastructure. Houthi forces threatened to target Jeddah and all Saudi Red Sea ports if Hodeidah is attacked; Defa Press claimed Saudi jets struck Sanaa airport and that drones hit Riyadh's Public Investment Fund tower.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz shipping attacks
threads.summary: UKMTO reported three vessels struck by unidentified projectiles on Monday while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, with Defa Press separately reporting a tanker hit. IRGC navy said an illegal cargo vessel north of Khassab struck a naval mine, and Iranian army air defence claimed it destroyed a US MQ-9 and a Lucas drone over the Persian Gulf.

threads.label: Israeli posture toward striking Iran
threads.summary: Defence Minister Israel Katz said Iran is developing chemical weapons and called for an IDF strike, preferably with US participation; Energy Minister Eli Cohen and former IAF commander Zvika Haimovich said Israel can strike Iran alone though US approval is preferable. NBC reported Trump administration officials are debating whether the US military should target senior Iranian leaders, while Trump said Iran had "little capacity to fire missiles."

threads.label: IRGC retaliation threats
threads.summary: IRGC Deputy Commander Gen. Izadi warned that any action against Iran's infrastructure or nuclear centres would bring destruction of regional infrastructure and operations beyond the region. Gen. Reza'i said Iran is determined to break the US blockade, and Foreign Minister Araghchi accused the US of "shamelessness" over alleged sabotage of the OPCW.

threads.label: Hamas internal security chief killed
threads.summary: The IDF and Shin Bet confirmed killing Naim Muhammad Ashour Abu Nahal, head of Hamas's internal security apparatus, in a Gaza City strike; Hamas's interior ministry confirmed the 50-year-old's death. Abu Nahal had assumed the role roughly two months ago after his predecessor Muein al-Arabid was captured by Israeli forces in September.

threads.label: Gaza disarmament and post-war posture
threads.summary: The Board of Peace announced Hamas and other Gaza factions had agreed to a roadmap to relinquish weapons and transfer authority to a transitional administration, though implementation remains limited. Defence Minister Katz said Israel will not permit rebuilding in Hamas-controlled Gaza or withdraw from the 65% of the Strip it holds absent disarmament, while Jared Kushner warned Israel faces "global-pariah status."

threads.label: Iran economic squeeze and domestic repression
threads.summary: Iran International reported Iran faces a year-end cash squeeze as US sanctions tighten on shadow banking, with growing disillusionment across political camps over Russian and Chinese support during the 2026 war. Singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four production team members received 74 lashes each over a YouTube concert without hijab, and parents in Sanandaj were arrested over the alleged killing of their pregnant daughter Helia Fattahi.

events.title: Two wanted Hamas operatives were nabbed by Israeli commandos during a raid in the northern west Bank overnight, the police say. Undercover Border Police officers arrived covertly to a building in the town of Salem, following intelligence provided by the Shin Bet on the location of the wanted men. The men are suspected of being involved in terror activities and advancing "military activity" for Hamas, according to the Shin Bet. Police say the officers breached the building and swiftly captured the two suspects, "with no unusual incidents."

events.title: Flogging of Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi sparks outrage on social media
events.summary: The flogging of Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her concert team on Monday sparked outrage on social media, with artists, activists and other users condemning the punishment and denouncing restrictions on women’s artistic expression in Iran.

events.title: Iraqi forces enter Iran-backed militia stronghold, but who holds power?
events.summary: Iraq’s deployment of government forces to Jurf al-Sakhar, a longtime stronghold of Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah, has raised questions about whether Baghdad can restore state authority or has merely reached a new compromise with powerful armed groups.

events.title: Tehran claims its missiles can reach Europe. What has it shown?
events.summary: An Iranian lawmaker’s claim that Tehran’s missiles can now travel 4,500 kilometers and a front-page boast by Tehran daily Hamshahri that all of Europe is within reach have renewed questions about Iran’s ability to strike the continent.
